# CS 27.917 — Design (rotor drive system)

> [!summary]
> CS 27.917 defines the rotor drive system of a small rotorcraft and sets three
> design rules for it. It is a CS-27 specification, not a CS-E one, and the
> rotorcraft applicant owns it. Each engine needs a unit that disengages it
> automatically on failure. The rotors needed for control in autorotation must
> keep turning after that disengagement. A torque limiting device, where used,
> must leave the pilot in control. The paragraph is about half the length of its
> CS-29 counterpart.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-27's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Incorporate in each rotor drive system a unit for each engine to automatically disengage that engine from the main and auxiliary rotors if that engine fails. | Required |
| **(b)** | Arrange each rotor drive system so that each rotor necessary for control in autorotation will continue to be driven by the main rotors after disengagement of the engine from the main and auxiliary rotors. | Required |
| **(c)** | Locate a torque limiting device, where one is used in the rotor drive system, so as to allow continued control of the rotorcraft when the device is operating. | Required |
| **(d)** | The rotor drive system includes any part necessary to transmit power from the engines to the rotor hubs: gear boxes, shafting, universal joints, couplings, rotor brake assemblies, clutches, supporting bearings for shafting, any attendant accessory pads or drives, and any cooling fans that are a part of, attached to, or mounted on the rotor drive system. | Statement |

Sub-point (d) imposes no action. It fixes what the other three sub-points, and
the additional tests of [ext CS 27.927], are about.

### Where CS-29 goes further

CS-27 states four sub-points. CS-29 states three lettered sub-points, one of
which carries six arrangement rules, and the difference is substantive rather
than editorial.

- **No design assessment.** CS 29.917(b) requires a design assessment of the
  rotor drive system, with a detailed failure analysis
  [ext CS 29.917(b)]. CS-27 has no counterpart. This is the largest of the
  differences, because the CS-29 loss-of-lubrication test takes its failure mode
  from that analysis [ext CS 29.927(c)]. It is set out in [[CS 29.917]].
- **The definition is narrower.** CS 27.917(d) ends its list with "any attendant
  accessory pads or drives, and any cooling fans that are a part of, attached
  to, or mounted on the rotor drive system" [ext CS 27.917(d)]. CS 29.917(a)
  inserts "lubricating systems for drive system gearboxes, oil coolers" before
  the cooling fans [ext CS 29.917(a)]. CS-27 does not name them; its list opens
  with "This includes" and is not exhaustive, so the omission is not an
  exclusion.
- **No multi-engine arrangement rule.** CS 29.917(c)(1) requires each rotor
  necessary for operation and control to continue to be driven by the remaining
  engines if any engine fails [ext CS 29.917(c)(1)]. CS-27 states no such rule.
- **The autorotation rule is unqualified.** CS 27.917(b) applies it to every
  rotorcraft. CS 29.917(c)(2) restricts the same sentence to single-engine
  rotorcraft [ext CS 29.917(c)(2)]. For the declared multi-engine installation
  the two codes therefore ask different things of the rotor drive system, and
  CS-27 asks the broader one here.
- **No intermeshing-rotor rules.** CS 29.917(c)(5) and CS 29.917(c)(6) govern
  the phase relationship of intermeshing rotors and a rotor dephasing device.
  Neither has a CS-27 counterpart.

### What CS-27 does not have

CS-27 publishes no AMC and no GM for point 27.917: [[CS 27.927]] records that a
search of CS-27 Amendment 10 returns nothing for it. CS-29 carries three AMCs
for its point 917, and one of them, AMC2 29.917, is the lubrication system
safety assessment set out in [[CS 29.917]].

An applicant certificating against CS-27 therefore has the four sub-points above
and no published means of complying with them.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 27.917 creates no CS-E obligation. It is a design rule for the rotor drive
system, which is not part of the engine type design. Two of its sub-points meet
the engine.

Sub-point (a) requires a unit that disengages the engine automatically when that
engine fails [ext CS 27.917(a)]. The unit is on the rotorcraft side of the
interface, but it acts on an engine failure. The rotorcraft applicant therefore
needs the engine failure conditions that trigger it. Those come from the safety
analysis of [[CS-E 510]] and reach the installer through the installation
instructions required by [[CS-E 20]].

Sub-point (c) is word for word CS 29.917(c)(4). Where the torque limiting
function sits in the full authority EECS declared in `engine_profile.md`, the
device is inside the engine type design: its integrity is engine-side evidence
under [[CS-E 50]], and its failure behaviour reaches [[CS-E 510]]. The open
question of which device the two codes mean is recorded in [[CS 29.917]].

The lubrication interface is empty on this side. CS-27 names no gearbox
lubricating system in its definition and sets no design assessment, so no
CS-27 obligation here consumes engine oil system data. The engine Oil System of
[[CS-E 570]] is a separate system in both codes.

Sub-points (b) and (d) create no engine data item at all. The autorotation
arrangement is a property of the drive train and the rotors, and the definition
imposes no action.

The airframe code is not fixed. [[CS-E 30]] carries that open item, and
[[CS 27.927]] records what turns on it for the rotor drive system tests.
